Resolves #20543

The Engine vs Frameworks section is where an evaluator decides, and five of its six pages closed by telling the reader when to stay with the other tool. Each conclusion now names the applications Neo.mjs builds, business apps included, and what it adds, and stays fair to the other library without making it the default. The ecosystem bullets keep the community-size fact and add the honest counterpoint. NeoVsNextJs stops gating Neo to "enterprise" SPAs and states its SEO support accurately.

Evidence: L1 (docs-only: relative links, whitespace, a phrase audit with a positive control) → L1 required (AC-1 to AC-4). No residuals.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | The `NeoVsReact.md`, `NeoVsVue.md`, `NeoVsAngular.md` and `NeoVsSolid.md` conclusions now position Neo.mjs for "the applications [their] teams build today, from everyday business apps to data-heavy dashboards", list what it adds (the components in one install, zero-build, an off-main-thread runtime, multi-window, the Neural Link) and end on the Getting Started guide. "Remains a viable / robust choice", "best-in-class … for standard business applications" and "a different class of problems" are gone |
| AC-2 | All four "Ecosystem & Maturity" bullets keep "its community is smaller" and add the counterpoint: those libraries ship a view layer and leave grids, forms, docking and routing to packages, while Neo.mjs ships them in one install (more than 450 classes) |
| AC-3 | `NeoVsNextJs.md`: the heading is "Interactive Applications of Every Size", with a business-applications bullet. The SEO row reads "Hydrates server-rendered markup (`useSSR`)" (`src/Main.mjs:530`, `src/worker/Manager.mjs:300`). The content-shell bullet became "Alongside an Existing Next.js Site", noting that neomjs.com's portal, docs and blog are a Neo.mjs application, and the conclusion no longer routes content sites away |
| AC-4 | `Overview.md:18` reads "The applications Neo.mjs builds, and what it adds on top". `check-relative-links.mjs`: OK. `check-whitespace.mjs`: exit 0 |

## Deltas from ticket
- **`NeoVsAngular.md`'s learning-curve bullet** said Neo has "an initial learning curve (especially its worker architecture)". That is the same discouraging pattern as #20519's §3, and it is untrue for application code: the engine runs the workers. It now names the few concepts to learn.
- **`NeoVsVue.md:5`'s intro** called Vue's model "best-in-class". That is dropped, consistent with the conclusion.
- **The SEO row states hydration, not built-in SSR:** the engine consumes `window.__NEO_SSR__`, and the server renderer lives outside this repository (the ticket's Avoided Trap).
- The technical comparison tables are unchanged, except NeoVsNextJs's stale SEO row.

## Test Evidence
Docs-only change, so there is no runtime surface. `node ./buildScripts/util/check-relative-links.mjs` and `node ./buildScripts/util/check-whitespace.mjs` pass. The phrase audit (`viable choice|robust choice|best-in-class|different class of problems|smaller but dedicated|might be the optimal|initial learning curve|requires pre-rendering`) finds 0 matches across `learn/comparisons/*.md`; its positive control, NeoVsExtJs's "technically superior successor", still matches. All three new link targets exist.
